prompt: Recall the key treatment/procedure steps for 2.01: Airway Management
answer:
2.01: Airway Management
Revised 01/22/2026
Overview
The purpose of advanced airway management is to safely secure a patient's airway while avoiding hypoxia,
hypotension, hypoventilation, aspiration or cardiac arrest.
During a crisis, a person does not rise to the occasion, but rather falls to the level of their training.
Learning a protocol will not build proficiency for intubation. SCEMSA supports focused monthly practice of
correct technique in simulation, acquiring feedback, correcting performance, and repetition that will build the
muscle memory necessary for the development of expertise.
Indication
◦ Airway protection or patency
◦ Failure of oxygenation or spontaneous ventilation
◦ Expected deterioration or in need of advanced airway management.
Contraindications
◦ Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is contraindicated in patients less than 2 years old.
◦ Avoid SGAs in situations with expected return of airway reflexes (e.g. when treating hypoglycemia or
narcotic OD), ingestion of caustic material, and airway burns.
Monitoring
◦ All patients before, during, and after airway management MUST be continuously monitored to include:
▪ EKG
▪ SpO2 and plethysmograph
▪ Waveform and qualitative Capnography
▪ Blood pressure/Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)

prompt: Recall the key treatment/procedure steps for 2.02: Airway – All Providers
answer:
2.02: Airway – All Providers
Revised 01/11/2026
Evaluate to Anticipate Difficulty and Potential Deterioration
Evaluate the patient's anatomy for:
▪ Anatomic difficulty
▫ Large incisors
▫ Small mandible
▫ Short neck
▫ Poor upper lip bite
▫ Clinical evaluation of anatomy is specific but lacks sensitivity in predicting difficulty, so always be
prepared
Health states
▫ C-spine arthritis
▫ Obesity
▫ Critically ill or high metabolic demand may desaturate rapidly.
▫ Disease of the oropharynx, neck or C-spine
• Including but not limited to cancer, esophageal varices, and prior radiation.
Evaluate the patient's physiology
Preoxygenation
Open the airway as needed.
▪ Conscious patients may assume position of comfort unless c-spine injury is suspected.
▪ Use a jaw-thrust or modified jaw-thrust if c-spine injury is suspected.
▪ Semi-conscious patients with an intact gag reflex shall have a nasopharyngeal airway inserted unless
contraindicated.
▪ Unresponsive patients without a gag reflex shall have an oropharyngeal airway inserted unless
contraindicated.
Pre-oxygenate.
▪ Utilize 2 sources of oxygen, including standard nasal cannula at ≥ 15 lpm for a minimum of 3 minutes,
targeting 100% oxygen saturations on all patients.
▪ Consider Delayed Sequence Intubation (DSI) with non-invasive ventilation (NIV) for hypoxia in altered,
agitated, or combative patients, or in patients with BMI > 30
Positioning
Position to optimize airway and oxygenation if no c-spine injury is suspected.
▪ At least 20 degrees elevation at the head of the bed (HOB)
▪ Ears to sternal notch, facial plane parallel to ceiling
▪ If excess secretions, vomitus, or blood, position to keep airway clear
Bag Valve Mask (BVM)
Utilize 2-person BVM technique unless resources are limited.
▪ Achieve a mask seal with the two thumbs down positioning.
▪ Utilize OPA/NPAs and jaw thrust to maintain an open airway.
▪ Consider utilizing pediatric BVM to avoid excessive ventilation volumes.
▪ Keep pressure below 20 cmH2O.

2.03: Airway - EMT & Above
Revised 01/04/2026
Supraglottic Airway (SGA) with endorsement for EMT
◦ Pre-oxygenate for 1-2 minutes with BVM prior to insertion and check for gag.
◦ Remove dentures/plates.

◦ Insertion

prompt: Recall the key treatment/procedure steps for 2.04: Airway - AEMT & Above (CPAP/NIV)
answer:
2.04: Airway - AEMT & Above (CPAP/NIV)
Revised 01/22/2026
Continuous airway pressure/non-invasive ventilation for patients with impending failure
Indications
◦ Conscious patients with severe respiratory distress due to:
▪ Congestive heart failure (CHF) with pulmonary edema
▪ Near-drowning with pulmonary edema
▪ Exacerbation of asthma
▪ Exacerbations of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
▪ Carbon monoxide poisoning
Relative contraindications
◦ Pediatric patients without appropriately-fitting equipment - use with caution.
◦ Unconscious or unable to self-maintain airway.
Contraindications
◦ Respiratory arrest or inadequate respiratory effort
◦ Facial trauma or deformities
◦ Penetrating chest trauma or pneumothorax
◦ Recent GI surgery or bleeding
◦ Persistent nausea/emesis
◦ SBP< 90mmHg
Procedure
◦ Initial settings: IPAP of 10 and EPAP of 5 with minimum pressure support (IPAP-EPAP of 5).
◦ Patients with increased work of breathing and hypercapnia: increase IPAP.
◦ Patients with hypoxia or pulmonary edema should have an increase in EPAP, maintaining a pressure
support of at least 5 as needed to meet clinical goals.
Notes
◦ Continuous ETCO2 monitoring MUST be performed on all non-invasive ventilation patients.
◦ Paramedic units MUST be enroute to the call before CPAP is applied by an AEMT.
◦ Advise receiving hospital of CPAP application ASAP so they can prepare.
◦ Monitor patient for gastric distension, which may lead to vomiting.
◦ For patients < 12 years old, use appropriate sized equipment and start at lower pressures: 2cm H20

answer:
2.07.01: Airway - Adult Cricothyrotomy
Revised 01/11/2026
Scope: Paramedic
Indications:
◦ Unconscious adult with immediate life-threatening airway compromise
◦ Other methods of airway management are ineffective or contraindicated
Contraindications:
◦ Patients less than 10 years old
◦ Inability to locate anatomical landmarks
Equipment:
◦ Scalpel
◦ Bougie
◦ 6.0 ETT (for most adults)
Identify Landmarks:
◦ The cricothyroid membrane is located midline on the anterior neck between the inferior thyroid cartilage
and above the cricoid ring.
Procedure:
◦ If sedation needed, follow Analgesia in the Non-Intubated Patient procedure and Sedation in the Non-
Intubated Patient procedure:

◦ Pad under the shoulders if no c-spine suspected (and time permits) to extend the neck.
◦ Make a vertical incision through the skin over the cricothyroid membrane 2-3 cm in length with sufficient
depth to expose the cricothyroid membrane.
◦ Horizontally puncture the cricothyroid membrane with the scalpel and access the trachea.
◦ Insert a cuffed endotracheal tube and advance cuff 2 cm past the opening.
◦ Verify placement by visualizing oropharynx to ensure tube is not misdirected.
◦ Verify patency with lung sounds, chest rise, SpO2, and ETCO2.
◦ Secure the tube.
◦ Refer to post-intubation management if on-going sedation is needed

prompt: Recall the key treatment/procedure steps for 2.07.02: Airway - Pediatric Needle Jet Ventilation
answer:
2.07.02: Airway - Pediatric Needle Jet Ventilation
Revised 01/11/2026
Scope: Paramedic
Indications:
◦ Unconscious pediatric with immediate life-threatening airway compromise
◦ Other methods of airway management are ineffective or contraindicated
Contraindications:
◦ Patients greater than 10 years old
◦ Inability to locate landmarks
Equipment:
◦ 15 mm adapter from a 3.0 tube or Jet Ventilator
◦ 12-16 gauge angiocatheter
Identify Landmarks:
◦ The cricothyroid membrane is located midline on the anterior neck between the inferior thyroid cartilage
and above the cricoid ring.
Procedure:
◦ If sedation needed, follow Analgesia & Sedation in the Non-Intubated Patient Procedure

◦ Draw up 2.5ml of Normal Saline with a 5ml syringe and attach to an appropriate gauge catheter-over-
needle device.
◦ Insert the needle through the cricothyroid membrane at a 45 to 60-degree caudal angle (toward the feet)
while aspirating for air.
◦ Ventilate through the catheter with BVM or jet device at highest concentration of oxygen until adequate
chest rise.
◦ Allow for adequate exhalation (OPA/NPA)
◦ Secure the catheter by hand until a better airway is placed.
◦ Verify patency with lung sounds, chest rise, SpO2, and ETCO2.
◦ Refer to post-intubation management if on-going sedation is needed
Ventilate:
◦ I:E ratio of 1:3
◦ Expect PaCO2 to rise by 2-4mmHg/minute.
◦ Consider OPA/NPA to allow for exhalation and relieve hypercapnea.
Titrate Pressure:
◦ Use minimum required to deliver tidal volume.
◦ Age <5 yrs: Use a BVM w/ a 3.0 ETT adapter.
Monitor for complications:
◦ Subcutaneous emphysema
◦ Barotrauma
◦ Catheter kinking
◦ Obstruction from blood or mucus
◦ Esophageal puncture
Citations
15: Manual of Emergency Airway Management, third edition, Ron Wall

3.05.01 : Cardiac Arrest - Adult
Revised 01/15/2026
Designation of Condition
Pulseless and apneic from a medical cause.
Tools
CPR Tool
Tempo: 110 compressions per minute
Cycle: 2 minutes
Reference: CPR Guidelines
All EMS Providers
◦ Early access to CPR and early defibrillation is critical to successful cardiac resuscitation. BLS personnel
should never wait for paramedic arrival before utilizing the AED. Also reference Dead at Scene Protocol.
◦ Est
ablish Primary Management.
◦ Orchestrate resuscitation as personnel allow. ALS care should follow current AHA ACLS cardiac arrest
guidelines when not otherwise specified in this document.
◦ High-performance CPR is the priority and is the preferred method for adult cardiac arrest. If not trained in
HPCPR, follow ACLS guidelines.
Multiple Rescuer
▫ CPR should be started immediately while the AED is applied and continued until the AED is ready to
analyze and shock. Deliver shock as soon as possible.
▫ Provide continuous compressions at a rate between 100-120 bpm for 2 minutes.
▫ The second rescuer should perform ventilations on every 10th upstroke of a compression for patients
who are not intubated.
▫ In the intubated patient breaths should be delivered every 6 seconds without attention to synchrony
with chest compressions. At no time should the provider performing compressions stop or pause for
ventilation.
Solo rescuer
▫ Compressions only at a ratio of 30:2
▫ If respiratory arrest is suspected cause for cardiac arrest or if not trained in HPCPR follow AHA
guidelines
▫ Integrate AED as available, utilizing pediatric pads/attenuator when appropriate.
◦ Perform 2 minutes of HPCPR, THEN check for rhythm/pulse.
▪ If no pulse: check rhythm and repeat defibrillation sequence as advised/indicated.
◦ The cycle is 2 minutes of CPR followed by rhythm check and one defibrillation (if needed) repeated until
resuscitation is successful or efforts terminated.

prompt: Recall the key treatment/procedure steps for 3.05.03: Refractory VF & pVT
answer:
3.05.03: Refractory VF & pVT
Revised 01/11/2026
Scope: Paramedic
Designation of Condition
Defibrillation for Refractory Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) and Pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia (pVT)
Background
◦ Double Sequential Defibrillation (DSD) and vector change (VC) are two defibrillation strategies for
refractory ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia.
◦ DSD is not synchronous.
▪ It is 2 separate shocks delivered as closely together as possible with separate pad placement.
▪ It is believed the different vectors provided by 2 sets of pads provide the benefit of the procedure. In
order to utilize DSD, it is important that common terminology is utilized and understood.
◦ The second strategy, vector change, can also benefit a patient not responding to traditional anterior-lateral
pad placement. In VC, the pads are changed from anterior-lateral to anterior-posterior for subsequent
shocks.
Key Definitions
◦ Refractory VF/pVT is defined as the rhythm never converting with defibrillation.
◦ Recurrent VF/pVT is a conversion with defibrillation but eventually deteriorating back to VF/pVT (i.e. VF >
PEA > VF > Asystole > VF)
◦ DSD and VC are only utilized for Refractory VF/pVT
Indication
VF/pVT Refractory to:
▪ 3 or more shocks, AND
▪ Administration of at least 1mg 1:10,000 Epinephrine (first round), AND
▪ Administration of at least 300mg of Amiodarone OR 1st dose of Lidocaine
Procedure
◦ Ensure adequate pad adherence and placement.
◦ Consider (1) DSD, or (2) Vector change defibrillation.
◦ If patient in VF/pVT from initial rhythm, ensure 2nd defibrillator is available for DSD (may need to add
another medic unit)
◦ Prepare site for attachment of additional set of external defibrillation pads. Must use 2 devices from the
same manufacturer. An AED may be used in manual mode as long as it is from the same manufacturer.
◦ Apply pads so that one set is anterior-lateral, and the other is anterior- posterior.
E

Overview
◦ Snohomish County EMS has adopted the WA State DOH standing order allowing EMS to dispense opioid
overdose reversal medications (naloxone) to any person at risk of experiencing an opioid-related overdose
or any person or entity in a position to assist a person at risk of experiencing an opioid-related overdose

will stress that persons MUST call 911 in addition to administering naloxone.
◦ It is important to keep in mind that the distribution of the Naloxone Leave Behind Kit is not the solution to
the overdose crisis but serves as a mechanism to begin conversations about access to care, treatment, and
recovery. To that end, it is important to professionally convey that treatment and recovery services are
available through the contact information found in the kit.

◦ The "Leave Behind" program may be utilized at the discretion of the EMS provider for

▪ Any scene where there is suspicion for opiate toxicity (regardless of use of naloxone)

underlying condition.

▪ Age >/= 60
▪ Cardiac history
▪ History of syncope while at rest (sitting, driving)
▪ Family history of sudden cardiac death
▪ Multiple syncopal episodes (at least 2 in 24 hours)

7.01: Communication and Notification Issues
Revised 01/04/2026
Radio Reports
Radio/Phone reports should be kept as brief as possible. A short, concise report can be given over the
radio/phone, followed by a more detailed report at the hospital. For critical medical and trauma patients, it is
important to provide a clear picture of the patient, though brevity is still important. Only include the patient’s
medical history if something in that history is pertinent and important in obtaining a medication or procedural
order. The purpose of the radio/phone report is to provide an opportunity for the receiving facility to activate
the appropriate resources and services given the patient presentation. It is also utilized to provide MEDICAL
CONTROL for medication/procedural requests. The receiving facility should be contacted at the earliest
available opportunity during critical care cases.
Radio Report Structure
◦ Identify yourself, your unit and request to speak with either a nurse for routine ALS and BLS patients, or a
physician for critical patients or MEDICAL CONTROL. Unless the receiving facility is totally overwhelmed;
reports are given to either an RN or MD.
◦ Age, sex, and condition of patient
◦ Chief complaint or reason for transport with brief pertinent medical history (one sentence if possible)
◦ Vital signs
◦ Pertinent treatment rendered.
◦ Estimated time of arrival
◦ All providers must request to speak directly to the ED physician in the following cases:
▪ STEMI
▪ Cricothyrotomy
▪ ALS request to transfer field call to RN car
▪ Anytime protocol indicates Contact MEDICAL CONTROL
▪ Patients requiring advanced airway measures
▪ Pediatric refusals <28 days or suspected BRUE
▪ All "Yellow" and "Red" Trauma patients
▪ Application of a Tourniquet
▪ Termination of resuscitation when indicated in TOR Protocol
▪ Any other requests/concerns per field provider discretion
▪ Any critically ill patient who appears to be having a life-threatening event

Indications
◦ Acute agitation, aggressive, or violent behavior preventing safe assessment, treatment, and/or transport.
Contraindications
◦ Acute sympathetic overload/acute sympathomimetic ingestion
◦ Lack of commercial restraints
Proper Equipment
◦ Commercial restraints
◦ Gurney
Procedure
◦ Establish need for physical restraint and verbalize plan with all involved personnel.
◦ Explain restraints to patient and appropriate bystanders.
◦ A minimum of 5 people is needed to safely apply 4-point restraints; one person per limb and the fifth
supporting the head/airway.
◦ Use minimum force necessary to apply restraints; avoid putting pressure on joints.
◦ Restraint the patient supine on the gurney.
◦ Secure restraints to frame of gurney, not to side rails.
◦ Use the fewest restraints necessary to achieve safety.
◦ Restrained extremities should be evaluated for pulse quality, capillary refill, color, temperature, nerve and
motor function immediately following application and at a minimum of every 15 minutes thereafter. Any
abnormal findings require adjustment, removal and reapplication of restraints if necessary. Assess and
document circulation, sensation, and movement distal to the restraints every 15 minutes while restraints are
in place.

prompt: Recall the key treatment/procedure steps for 7.14.02: Ultrasound - Cardiac Arrest Pulse Check
answer:
7.14.02: Ultrasound - Cardiac Arrest Pulse Check
Revised 01/21/2026
Scope: Paramedics with MPD Specialized Training
Cardiac Evaluation and Pulse Check POCUS for Cardiac Arrest
Indications:
◦ Cardiac Arrest
 Contraindications:
◦ Other resuscitative efforts
 Procedure
Pulse checks should remain < 5 seconds and should NEVER interfere with CPR or defibrillation.
▪ At appropriate intervals, save image and record incident number in software
▪ Personnel are in place focusing on high-performance CPR and resuscitation per ACLS algorithms.
▪ The ultrasound-trained paramedic will determine whether ultrasound is indicated.
▪ Position probe on the selected anatomical landmark while CPR is ongoing to reduce time off the chest.
▫ Parasternal long or sub-xyphoid for cardiac motion assessment
• Carotid or femoral for POCUS pulse check
▪ At designated times, compressions are paused for a rhythm check.
▫ If a shockable rhythm is present, do not delay defibrillation to obtain ultrasound image.
▪ Follow ACLS guidelines. Perform immediate defibrillation.
• Simultaneously, during rhythm check, there should be an initial POCUS pulse check at the carotid
artery or femoral artery.
▪ If no POCUS pulse seen continue CPR per standard protocol.
▪ If a pulse is present, check for palpable central pulse.
▪ If palpable central pulse present, start ROSC care.
▪ If no palpable central pulse, continue CPR starting fluids, vasopressors. On the next pulse
check, scan for cardiac activity.
▪ Prepare during CPR in the subxiphoid view so when the pulse check occurs you are set to
image and record taking less than 5 seconds. Ideally the pulse checks should be timed.
▪ Compressions should not be delayed for ultrasound imaging. If an image cannot
be acquired in <5 seconds, resume compressions.
▪ If cardiac activity is noted, continue CPR until the next pulse check.
▪ Check for the POCUS pulse and if present check for a palpable central pulse.

Revised 01/23/2026

Indications
◦ Hemorrhagic shock due to:
▪ Acute trauma
▪ Post-partum hemorrhage/vaginal bleeding
▪ Contact Medical Control for other hemorrhagic conditions who meet vitals criteria:
▫ Systolic BP <70mmHg regardless of heart rate
▫ Systolic BP <90 and HR greater than 110.
Contact
Online Medical Control
Phones: Online Medical Control: 425-404-5099
Note: Providence Everett - Colby Campus shall be contacted for all online medical
control requests, regardless of final destination.
▪ EMS Witnessed traumatic circulatory arrest within 10 minutes of PRMCE.
Contraindications
◦ Known personal or religious objection to blood products
◦ Unwitnessed cardiac arrest
Proper equipment
◦ Whole Blood or blood component
◦ Blood tubing
◦ Blood warmer
◦ Normal Saline
▪ Do not use Lactated Ringer's to prime blood tubing
Procedure
Prime Blood Tubing
▪ Establish IV/IO access with largest bore IV possible (18g+ preferred)
▪ Open blood tubing and close all roller clamps
▪ Remove spike protector end cap. Insert one spike into Normal Saline bag and open roller clamp on that
line. Keep vent cap closed
▪ Invert filter chamber. Partially open roller clamp downstream of filter chamber. Allow approximately 3/4
of the chamber to fill with Normal Saline. DO NOT SQUEEZE CHAMBER. Close downstream roller clamp
once 3/4 full.
▪ With filter chamber still inverted, partially open roller clamp on unused lead, prime, then close roller
clamp.
▪ Return filter chamber to upright position and clear trapped air. Slowly open downstream roller clamp to
prime, purging air and filling tubing with Normal Saline. Ensure air bubbles are removed.
▪ Attach blood tubing to IV/IO site and ensure luer lock is firmly connected.
▫ Do not use extension set or MicroClave connector. Connect blood tubing directly to IV/IO hub.
▪ Slowly open lower roller clamp and ensure patency; set to desired flow rate
